I have an MQB car running HCA5 (torque) coming from the legacy model notre dame. 

First of all, OP long on SL3v2 is really, really good. Very smooth, very human-like, and it actually gives you some confidence that it will brake, unlike stock ACC which is kinda nerve-wracking to drive with (it does always stop, and very smooth, but does it in a robotic way that makes you feel like the car might not stop). 

Regarding lat on the highway, SL3v2 has noticeably superior steering torque. I can actually take 90% of highway curves without running out of torque. It also steers very smoothly in general. 

Regarding lat in the city, SL3v2 is noticeably worse than ND. ND will actually take right and left turns with no intervention about 85% of the time, whereas SL3v2 is almost never able to make 90 degree turns without intervention. It always seems to not turn tight enough, and once it does figure out that it needs to turn tighter, it does not return to center and will try to run the car into the nearest curb.

If I could magically choose which model to have when, it’d be 

City lat: ND
City long: SL3v2

Highway lat: SL3v2
Highway long: SL3v2
My wife says I need a toggle for gaslighting
Well I mean technically one model is only using 45% of the GPU:P
What is HCA5?

The steering protocol we use to steer the car. It’s an internal Volkswagen name for “heading control assist 5”, AKA “lane keeping assistant 5”. 

I make this distinction because PQ (mk6 gen cars) use HCA7, which has significantly higher usable torque.

HCA status 5 allows less torque and is the stock LKAS signals used by every PQ/MQB Volkswagen vehicle
